cases.question: How will the air be tonight?
cases.answer:
Tonight (Wed 04 Nov 18:00 to 23:00), Karachi's air quality is forecasted to be Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, with PM2.5 predicted between 41.5 and 77.5 µg/m³ (AQI 115 to 139) during early evening and 36.4 to 81.7 µg/m³ (AQI 124) by 23:00. 

Live track record shows an overall MAE of 7.6 µg/m³, beating CAMS in 59 of 62 days, and backtest MAE at 24 hours is 5.0 µg/m³.

cases.answer:
PM2.5 is expected to peak on Thursday, 05 Nov 08:00 at 71.3 µg/m³, with an AQI category of Unhealthy. The 80% range (p10 to p90) for that hour is 62.6 to 90.8 µg/m³. 

Our live track record shows strong performance with an overall MAE of 7.6 µg/m³, beating CAMS in 59 of 62 recent evaluation days.

cases.question: Is tomorrow morning okay for a run outside?
cases.answer:
Tomorrow morning (Thursday, Nov 5) at 07:00, the AQI is predicted to be 159 (Unhealthy), with an 80% range for PM2.5 from 50.6 to 75.9 µg/m³. 

Live track record shows recent 13-24 hour forecasts have an MAE of 6.5 µg/m³, beating CAMS in 59 of 62 days. Given the Unhealthy air quality, you may want to skip or reschedule your outdoor run.

cases.question: How sure is the forecast for 48 hours from now?
cases.answer: For the 25-48h lead time, the live track record shows an MAE of 7.9 and skill vs CAMS of 41.1%. In backtesting at 48 hours, the MAE is 5.7 with an 80% range coverage of 86.0%.

cases.question: How accurate has this forecast actually been?
cases.answer: Our published forecasts have an overall Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 7.6 µg/m³, beating CAMS on 59 of 62 days with an overall skill score of 0.428. Rolling-origin backtests show consistent performance across lead times, with an MAE of 2.5 µg/m³ at 1 hour and 5.7 µg/m³ at 72 hours, while the 80% uncertainty range achieves an overall coverage of 76.4%.

cases.question: Is this better than the Copernicus CAMS forecast?
cases.answer: Yes, it outperforms CAMS. Its live track record shows it has beaten CAMS in accuracy on 59 of 62 days, achieving an overall skill score of 42.8% versus CAMS across all lead times.

cases.question: What is the backtested error at 72 hours?
cases.answer: At 72 hours, the backtested mean absolute error (MAE) is 5.741, with an $R^2$ of 0.612 and an 80% range coverage of 87.7%.

cases.question: How good is the 1-hour forecast?
cases.answer: For the live track record (1-6 hour bucket), the MAE is 5.6 with a skill vs CAMS of 0.599 and skill vs persistence of 0.339. In the backtest at the 1-hour lead time, the MAE is 2.5 with an R2 of 0.921, skill vs CAMS of 0.718, skill vs persistence of 0.089, and an 80% range coverage of 84.2%.

cases.question: Why does the model use CAMS as an input if CAMS is wrong?
cases.answer: Even though CAMS can be inaccurate on its own, it serves as a useful raw signal that provides the model with large-scale meteorological and pollution transport patterns. The live track record shows our forecasts beat CAMS by 42.8% overall (winning 59 of 62 days), with a live MAE of 7.6 compared to CAMS's 13.3. In the backtest, our model achieves a mean skill vs CAMS of 45.8% by correcting those errors using local ground data.
